open_questions: Stellar variability strong (amplitude 4630-8214 ppm) leaves shape measurement uncertain but phase-curve amplitude 257.6 ppm (ratio 0.04771) shows no large out-of-transit swing

High impact parameter (fit_b 0.9742) and V sigma 1.968 keep blend at faint Gaia neighbours (closest that could 34.1 arcsec needs 0.01 eclipse) possible in principle but no off-target centroid to support it
dossier.public_summary: A 12.8-day, 4.4 Earth-radius dip repeats steadily in three transits on a dim M-dwarf with no odd-even mismatch or secondary eclipse, consistent with a small planet. The shape is flat-bottomed despite strong spot variability, and the duration matches the star's size even allowing for a grazing geometry. No neighbour within one pixel can plausibly mimic the dip.

reasons.why: Planet-sized (much below 10 REarth) strongly favours a planet over a small star.
No significant odd/even depth difference (odd 4976 ppm vs even 5515 ppm) - no preference for EB at twice period.
No significant secondary eclipse (snr 2.636 <5 and below brightening) and no secondary at half-phase - disfavours equal-mass EB; primary depth consistent with irradiation for giant planet.
Depth steady between sectors (5537 ppm and 4411 ppm) despite low SNR, with transit_depths p_consistent 0.270 - not driven by one bad/brightening transit.
Observed 1.999 h vs central 2.741 h (TIC) and 0.67-0.73 with Gaia radii (0.561, 0.557 Rsun) fits central with high impact parameter, consistent with planet geometry.
